analysis:
Examined: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head 1310-1821; the actual changes are the date bump at line 3 and line 52, which now states that GLM video accepts constant or variable frame-rate mp4/quicktime inline data URLs). The rest of the excerpt is unchanged surrounding text: update, beta, fan, logout, report, paths and passthrough env.

The test file GLM5NextMediaRoutingTests.swift (head 94-137 and 256-309) adds a marker tokenizer and an OpenRouter readiness test. The test loads SHA-256-pinned video fixtures from the libs/mlx-swift-lm test resources and expects VFR QuickTime and MP4 inputs to reach the engine instead of failing as invalid_media. It is test-only, with no production attack surface.

The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule moves 7bed8216 -> 6aef0a5d. Its diff is not supplied. It likely changes video decode or sampling to accept variable-frame-rate clips; the test expects grids [11,40,108] and [5,52,92]. This widens the decoder input accepted from adversarial consumers (ADV-002), whose decrypted media is plaintext A-001 inside the provider process (TB-007, T-050 temp-file exposure).

Unverified and needing integration review:
- Does the VFR path keep the bounded ingest limits (max duration, decoded bytes, frame count) and the GLM5NextVisionBudget reservation?
- Does decoding stay in memory, or does it write plaintext temp files (T-050)?
- Are malformed VFR timestamps (zero or negative deltas, huge durations) bounded, so they cannot cause CPU or memory DoS?

No concrete regression is visible in the supplied evidence. Missing submodule source is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
